statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail sits in the low band and well below the block threshold because the observed NQ price path is a narrow, two-sided overnight range, while Stress stays elevated on the US-Iran energy escalation, a 10-year Treasury yield of 4.758% and a live debate about a September Federal Reserve rate hike.
recommendation: Conditions are described as ordinary in price-path terms but materially stressed in macro terms. A narrow evidence-based caution window is mapped from 13:30 to 16:00 UTC, covering the US cash open, the 14:00 UTC ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS pair and the first hour of repricing, where the forecast policy state steps to WATCH for two clock-hours before returning to EA_ON.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold a 47-point overnight range while oil, a 4.76% 10-year yield and a live September rate-hike debate carry the macro stress
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed 31 August at 29,456.97, up 0.08% inside a 29,304.49-29,483.90 session range, outperforming the S&P 500 (-0.33%) and the Dow (-0.70%). NQ futures are at 29,480.75, down 0.11%, inside a Globex range of 29,475.00-29,522.50 - a two-sided span of about 47.5 points that shows no directional efficiency, no repeated extension and no failed-retracement sequence. ES futures are effectively unchanged at 7,698.50 and VIX is 14.92. The macro backdrop is far more stressed than the price path. US forces struck Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island, Iran responded against American positions in Jordan, and threats have been extended to the Kharg Island export hub; WTI settled 2.83% higher at $85.76 and trades near $86.42, with Brent settling at $90.49. Separately, Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh used Jackson Hole to warn that inflation is not slowing sufficiently, and futures now price roughly a 58-62% probability of a September rate hike. That has driven a bear steepening: the 2-year is at 4.36%, the 5-year at 4.507%, the 10-year at 4.758% and the 30-year above 5.20%. Latest-session index internals were rotational rather than directional, with semiconductors broadly higher and several megacaps lower, which dilutes the conditions needed for persistent one-way index structure. Under the repository mapping this combination produces low Tail with elevated Stress. The scheduled catalysts today are Fed Barr at 13:05 UTC, the S&P Global manufacturing PMI final at 13:45 UTC, and ISM Manufacturing (consensus 55.2 against 55.6 prior) together with JOLTS (consensus about 7.33M against 7.359M prior) at 14:00 UTC, ahead of ADP on 2 September, ISM Services and Fed Waller on 3 September and August payrolls on 4 September.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment. Tail stayed between 5 and 17 across 31 August and into the overnight session, with the policy state mapped to EA_ON in every hour. Stress climbed from the high-30s during the Asian session to the low-to-mid 50s once the Gulf escalation, the oil move and the long-end yield rise were absorbed through European and US hours, and it has since held near 50-53. Dominant mode was mixed apart from an event/whipsaw phase around 09:00-10:00 UTC, and confidence ranged from 84 to 88.
outlookSummary: The base case is a continuation of ordinary, two-sided conditions through the remaining Asian and European hours, with conditional Tail easing to 8 in the quietest windows. Risk concentrates on the 13:00-16:00 UTC block covering the Fed Barr remarks, the 13:30 UTC cash open and the 14:00 UTC ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS pair, where forecast Tail peaks at 21 and the mapped policy state steps to WATCH for two clock-hours before decaying back into the low band through the US afternoon. A secondary checkpoint sits at the 19:00 UTC power hour and at the post-close Palo Alto Networks and Dell reports. Stress stays in the low-fifties to low-sixties across the whole horizon because oil, the long end of the Treasury curve and the September rate-hike question are all unresolved into ADP, ISM Services and August payrolls later this week.

forecast.analysis: Observed now: NQ futures 29,480.75 (-0.11%) inside a 47.5-point Globex range of 29,475.00-29,522.50, two-sided with no directional efficiency, and ES essentially flat. VIX is 14.92. The stress sits in cross-asset macro - the 10-year at 4.758% and WTI back above $86 - rather than in the index price path.
